executive_summary.headline: Google ships a #1-ranked model and makes Gemini a file editor
executive_summary.body: Gemini 4 Carbon tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59 and launches at $2 in and $10 out per million tokens, while the Gemini app now creates, previews and edits documents, PDFs, slides and spreadsheets in chat. Genie 4 adds native audio to generated worlds. Carbon and Genie 4 are limited-access at launch.

executive_summary.headline: Creators and small businesses get agents that finish the work
executive_summary.body: Riverside Agents produce, edit, clip and post video, Canva Brush edits whole decks from one prompt, and Empacer, the week's top Product Hunt launch with a score of 453, lets small business owners speak a task and approve the result.

executive_summary.headline: Claude reports real lab numbers from drug discovery
executive_summary.body: Anthropic's partners report a CAR T domain redesign about 70% shorter with roughly 10 times the receptors, 1,010 antibody variants tested in about 10 weeks, and an 89% cut in document review time. A day later it added 20 science partners and free Claude credits.

executive_summary.headline: Open weights get bigger and smaller at once
executive_summary.body: Mistral Large 4 puts a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model on Hugging Face at $0.70 in and $2.10 out per million tokens, while Liquid AI's LFM3 packs six 2B-class models that fit single-GPU fine-tuning.

executive_summary.headline: Fun finds: talking haunted garages and group-chat dinner bookers
executive_summary.body: NVIDIA shows a Halloween garage door that answers back in about 1.7 seconds using open Nemotron models, and Zest books restaurant tables for a whole group chat over text.

top_picks.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model for long-horizon agentic work
top_picks.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 with a score of 59, per Google, and is built for long-running agentic tasks. Launch pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, rising to $4 and $20 after the introductory period. Access starts with a subset of cyber defenders and trusted partners through the Fairwind Program, with broader developer, business and consumer access planned.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: line up the one long, multi-step job you keep postponing, such as a full market scan or a codebase migration, so it is ready to run the day broader access opens.
top_picks.competitive_context: Google reports a #1 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score (59) and #4 on WebDev Arena (1768, +89 Elo). The cached-input discount is 95%. Access is gated at launch, so hands-on comparison against Gemini 4 Argon and rival frontier models comes later.
top_picks.pricing: $2 / $10 per million input / output tokens at launch; $4 / $20 after the introductory period; cached input 95% off.
key_takeaways: Ranked #1 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 (59), per Google.
Introductory price of $2 in / $10 out per million tokens.
Rollout begins with trusted partners, then developers, businesses and consumers.

top_picks.title: Gemini now creates, previews and edits documents, PDFs, slides and spreadsheets inside the chat
top_picks.summary: Gemini can generate a file, preview it and edit it in place: type changes, highlight text to ask questions, or have Gemini refine it. PDF preview and editing work on web and mobile; Docs, Sheets, slide decks, Markdown, TXT and code are web-only. It is available to all users in every language where the Gemini app runs.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: drop last quarter's messy report PDF into Gemini and ask for a one-page slide version, then edit the slides by highlighting and typing.
top_picks.competitive_context: Claude shipped Docs and Slides in beta in September; Gemini's edit-in-chat reaches every Gemini app user without a paid-plan requirement stated.
top_picks.pricing: Available to all Gemini app users; no price stated.
key_takeaways: Edit files in full-screen view by typing or highlighting text.
PDF editing on web and mobile; other formats on web.
No paid-plan requirement stated.

top_picks.title: Empacer lets small business owners talk to an assistant that drafts posts, replies and invoices
top_picks.summary: Empacer asks three setup questions, then turns spoken requests into finished work: customer replies, social posts, invoices and a first week of drafted content. Nothing is sent without the owner's approval. It topped the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard with a score of 453 and 84 comments, and runs in a browser and on Android, with iOS listed as coming soon.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: set up a hands-free assistant for your own week: say what you need aloud on a commute and review the drafts when you sit down.
top_picks.competitive_context: Competes with general chat assistants by removing the prompt step; the makers say it uses LiveKit voice isolation so it works in noisy shops.
top_picks.pricing: Free options listed; 60% off the first subscription period for Product Hunt visitors; 3-day trial via Google Play. Subscription prices not shown.
key_takeaways: Three-question onboarding, then a drafted first week of work.
1000+ integrations, per the maker.
Approval required before anything is sent.

top_picks.title: Canva Brush edits existing designs from a single prompt, one slide or a whole deck
top_picks.summary: Brush is a vision-language model from Canva Research that restyles designs, changes multi-page designs with one prompt and remixes designs for other channels, with fully editable output. Canva says it is up to 69% faster and 46% cheaper per edit task than its previous design agent. It powers supported design edits in Canva AI for Pro subscribers starting October 29, with wider availability coming.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: take your best-performing campaign graphic and ask Brush to remix it for four channels in one pass.
top_picks.competitive_context: Canva Craft arrived last week as an image model; Brush is the editing counterpart, so generation and revision now both live inside Canva.
top_picks.pricing: Included for Canva Pro subscribers on supported edits; no separate price stated.
key_takeaways: Up to 69% faster and 46% lower cost per edit task, per Canva.
One prompt can change every page of a deck.
Select Brush in the Canva AI dropdown.

top_picks.title: Anthropic reports lab results from Claude-driven drug discovery with six research partners
top_picks.summary: Scientists at Generate Biomedicines used Claude Code to redesign a CAR T-cell signaling domain that came out about 70% shorter with roughly 10 times as many surface receptors. BigHat Biosciences tested about 1,010 antibody variants in about 10 weeks, and Enveda cut manufacturing-document review time 89%, from over 25 hours to under 3. Anthropic also reports a Claude Science workbench, Claude credits for life scientists and an open call for guest investigators.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: pick one slow lab review task, such as a methods document or a batch of variant results, and time how long Claude takes against your current baseline.
top_picks.competitive_context: Closest peers are OpenAI's GPT-Rosalind and its academic plan from recent weeks; Anthropic's pitch here is named partner results with measured numbers.
top_picks.pricing: Claude credits for life scientists; no prices stated.
key_takeaways: Enveda: 1,061 pages reviewed, review time down 89%.
Divergence Labs: about 35,000 antibody designs in about a month.
Work is mostly preclinical, per Anthropic.

top_picks.title: Mistral releases Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter open-weight model
top_picks.summary: Mistral Large 4 is natively multimodal, offers Low, Medium and High reasoning modes and scores 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, per Mistral. It is priced at $0.70 per million input tokens and $2.10 per million output tokens, with weights on Hugging Face under a modified MIT license. It is also available through Mistral Studio, OpenRouter, Microsoft Foundry and NVIDIA-hosted endpoints.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: swap it into your favorite coding agent for an afternoon and compare cost per finished task against your current model.
top_picks.competitive_context: Mistral says it uses 47% fewer tokens per task than the leading open-weight model. Hugging Face lists weights the same day.
top_picks.pricing: $0.70 / $0.07 cached / $2.10 per million input / cached / output tokens; weights free under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight license.
key_takeaways: 1T-parameter open-weight multimodal model.
Weights run on vLLM or SGLang.
Model-as-a-Service businesses need a separate commercial license.

top_picks.title: Riverside launches four video agents that produce, edit, clip and post for creators
top_picks.summary: Riverside Agents are a Producer, Editor, Clipper and Marketer that take a recording from prep to published clips. They remove pauses and filler, add captions and branding, and schedule posts, and nothing publishes without the creator's approval. They are included in every Riverside plan with a 14-day free trial; Product Hunt listed 167 points on launch day.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: feed one long internal talk or webinar recording to the Clipper and see how many shareable minute-long highlights come back.
top_picks.competitive_context: Sits between all-in-one editors and general agents: agents built only for video, living inside the recording tool itself.
top_picks.pricing: Included in every Riverside plan, features vary by plan; AI-credit features still draw credits; 14-day free trial.
key_takeaways: Four agents: Producer, Editor, Clipper, Marketer.
Approval required before publishing.
Phone-based clip review.

top_picks.title: Genie 4 generates playable worlds with native audio and real-time steering
top_picks.summary: Genie 4 produces interactive worlds with ambient sound and spoken dialogue, and you can steer a simulation in real time with natural-language prompts or keyboard controls. Gemini Omni anchors real-world appearance and Gemini 3.8 Flash guides multi-step tasks. It is in research preview for trusted testers, with Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early-access API partners next.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: describe your office lobby, a factory floor or a favorite childhood place in a paragraph and see what world comes back when access opens.
top_picks.competitive_context: Google's generated video and audio carry SynthID watermarks. No price is stated.
key_takeaways: Native audio including dialogue.
Steer worlds with text prompts in real time.
Trusted testers now; Ultra subscribers and API partners next.

sections.title: Product Hunt
sections.description: Top AI launches of the week by Product Hunt score. Maker site first, Product Hunt page second. Empacer, Canva Brush and Riverside Agents also launched there and appear in Top Picks.

items.title: Vaani Developer Platform
items.summary: Vaani builds voice agents without code: design the call flow, handle objections and edge cases, connect your tools and knowledge base, and go live on a real phone number. Every call ends with structured data. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: build a missed-call answering agent for a simple scenario, like store hours and booking requests, and measure how many calls it resolves.

items.title: TheySaid 4.0
items.summary: TheySaid turns surveys into conversations: point it at a URL or document and the AI trains in under a minute, then your audience can answer and ask questions as if talking to you. Version 4.0 adds a way to see how users will react right where you build. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: swap one static customer survey for a conversational one and compare completion rates.

items.title: Strawberry 1.0
items.summary: Strawberry is a browser with built-in AI companions that learn your preferences and workflows and can work for you around the clock. The maker's tagline claims it saves teams more than 100 hours a week. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: hand one weekly browser chore, like pulling competitor pricing, to a companion and see what it handles unattended.

items.title: Knocket AI
items.summary: Knocket adds free live chat to a website or app, or turns your bio link into a personal contact page, and visitors can chat without signing up. It is built for founders, creators and small teams. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: turn your link-in-bio into a chat page and see what people actually ask.

items.title: Screen Studio 4.0
items.summary: Screen Studio 4.0 adds Glass Loupe, split-screen layouts including vertical video, edit-by-transcript, a background-free camera cutout, automatic hiding of sensitive data and faces, and exports up to 4x faster. It is a Mac screen recorder that auto-zooms on clicks and smooths mouse movement. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: record a two-minute product walkthrough and edit it by deleting words from the transcript.
items.pricing: 20% off the first year of a yearly plan with code HELLOHUNTERS through November 8.

items.title: Scape
items.summary: Scape is an email client that prioritizes messages, prepares contextual drafts and tracks follow-ups, drawing on your email, meetings, calendar and attachments. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: start Monday with an inbox already sorted and replies drafted, then judge the time saved by Wednesday.

items.title: SpeakON Agent
items.summary: SpeakON Agent turns spoken requests into completed work across connected iPhone apps: drafting emails, scheduling meetings and sharing updates, with you approving what goes out. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: dictate your next three follow-up emails and a meeting request in one breath.
items.recurrence_note: The SpeakON dictation app was listed in an earlier week; this is the new Agent product.

items.title: Overmind
items.summary: Overmind is an open-source platform that turns production traces into specialised models you own, trained, benchmarked and served. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: export one noisy agent's traces and see whether a small tuned model matches it for a fraction of the cost.

items.title: Dedica
items.summary: Dedica runs 125 free checks to test whether AI agents can browse, compare and sign up on your website, then gives a fix for each failure to hand to your coding agent. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run it on your own site this afternoon and fix the top three agent-blocking issues.

items.title: Precise Edit by Ideogram
items.summary: Precise Edit gives Ideogram 4.5 a context window for editing images at original resolution up to 8K, for recoloring products, repairing logos and replacing or removing objects with sharper small text. It is in the app and the API, and the Product Hunt listing shows 132 points.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: fix the one logo or product shot you keep avoiding and compare against your usual editor.
items.pricing: API pricing of $0.008 to $0.22 per image, per the Product Hunt listing.

sections.title: Frontier and Open Models
sections.description: New model releases beyond the Top Picks (Gemini 4 Carbon, Mistral Large 4, Genie 4).

items.title: Liquid AI releases LFM3, six small open models for text, vision, audio and decisions
items.summary: LFM3 is a family of six 2B-class open-weight models built on a 1.7B base with a 256K-token context, pretrained on 22T tokens. They are designed for single-GPU fine-tuning and edge deployment, and the text model fits in about 1 GB at 4-bit precision.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: fine-tune the text model on your own notes on one GPU and run it offline on a laptop.

items.title: AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel bring open speech and decision models to Apple devices
items.summary: AnySpeechRecognizer lets Swift developers pick local engines like Parakeet and Qwen3-ASR with speaker diarization for up to four speakers; Parakeet transcribes an hour of audio in about 20 to 40 seconds from a file. AnyDecisionModel returns yes/no, multiple-choice and rating decisions with probabilities. Packages need Swift 6.2 and macOS 26 or iOS 26.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: build a private meeting-transcript app for your Mac that never leaves the device.

items.title: IBM Granite Switch 4.1.1 updates speech and decision adapters without migration
items.summary: Granite Switch 4.1.1 is a patch release that retrains Granite Speech for speech-to-text in 10 languages with native punctuation and a refreshed Decision adapter, while the base model stays unchanged. It is backward compatible with 4.1.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: swap the new speech model into an existing transcription script and compare punctuation quality.

sections.title: YC and Startups
sections.description: Launch YC and Launch HN companies from the week. Confetti's date comes from the page listing; the YC page shows only relative times.

items.title: Confetti (YC F26) designs and orders hardware projects from plain-English prompts
items.summary: Confetti lets anyone describe a hardware idea while agents handle CAD, parts sourcing, wiring help and firmware, then submits supported 3D-printing jobs to print farms. Early users are building a portable mechanical analyzer for a physics lab, a custom keyboard, desk companions and gifts. The Launch YC page displays 106 points.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask it for a custom bracket or sensor mount you would otherwise wait weeks to get designed.

items.title: Simantic (YC F26) simulates firmware so AI agents can test it without hardware
items.summary: Simantic provides virtual development boards you can program from a terminal with one API call, plus an AI firmware reviewer and a CI pipeline that validates firmware on simulated microcontrollers. The founders say they built a deterministic simulation engine in Rust. The Launch HN post has 78 points and 36 comments.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: let a coding agent iterate on embedded code overnight against virtual boards instead of a bench.

sections.title: Consumer, Creator and Small Business
sections.description: Everyday AI features, fun finds and small-organization tools worth trying this month.

items.title: Zest's text-message agent finds restaurants and books tables for your group chat
items.summary: Zest's concierge works over text and can join a group chat, blend everyone's tastes, run an in-thread vote and book through OpenTable, Resy and SevenRooms. It personalizes with food and drink transactions imported through Plaid. The company was founded in November 2024 and raised $1.8 million pre-seed.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run your next team dinner vote in a group text and let the agent book the winner.

items.title: Gemini Notebook adds hundreds of free textbooks as grounded sources
items.summary: Students can add hundreds of textbooks from OpenStax, Open Textbook Library and S Chand Publishing to a notebook at no charge. Answers are grounded in the book with inline citations and direct links, and content turns into study guides, quizzes and flashcards.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: load a physics or materials textbook and generate a quiz to brush up before a technical review.

items.title: Gemini adds immersive explorations, interactive visual lessons from planets to atoms
items.summary: The Gemini student hub now has a library of interactive scenes on topics like the Silk Road, jet engines and lightning, where you tap labels to zoom from planetary scales down to molecules and atoms. Audio narration is planned, and direct access in chat is coming soon.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: open the jet engine scene and use it to explain heat flow to a curious colleague.

items.title: Chrome autofill now pulls order numbers and flight details from Gmail
items.summary: Chrome's enhanced autofill uses Gemini with Personal Intelligence to suggest order numbers, tracking details and flight bookings from Gmail when you fill out forms. It is rolling out in the U.S. on desktop, Android and iOS to Gemini in Chrome users who have Personal Intelligence enabled.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: file your next return or warranty form and see how many fields fill themselves.

items.title: A haunted garage that talks back: NVIDIA shows MonsterHouse built on open Nemotron models
items.summary: MonsterHouse is a Halloween projection that listens to visitors and answers as a grumpy pirate while animating a garage door as its mouth. It chains Nemotron ASR, a 4 GB Bolt model, Magpie TTS and Audio2Face-3D, with median speech-to-audio latency of 1.70 seconds, or 0.72 seconds for cached replies. The code is not released, but the models are available.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: give a lobby display or a conference-booth mascot a voice and a personality using the same pipeline.

items.title: Claude for Nonprofits adds a fundraising, marketing and hiring plugin with seats from $3
items.summary: The plugin bundles skills built with about 30 nonprofits for funder research, grant evaluation, proposals, donor relationships, marketing and hiring, and installs automatically on Team and Enterprise plans at no extra cost. Team's minimum drops to two people, discounts reach up to 75%, and verified nonprofits in low- and middle-income countries can pay about $3 per user per month.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: copy the skill structure for a small team of your own: one folder of grant-style templates the whole group can call.

sections.title: Enterprise AI
sections.description: Platform launches from the large vendors, kept short.

items.title: Microsoft Copilot adds more than 25 finance skills for accounting and capital markets
items.summary: Copilot gains skills for reconciliation, journal entries and reporting, plus Capital Markets and Finance plugins for multistep workflows in Cowork. In seven days of limited Insiders access, more than 8,000 users invoked accounting skills over 44,000 times, per Microsoft. Finance skills in Excel are generally available.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask an Excel accounting skill to reconcile one month of a small ledger and see how many exceptions it flags first.

items.title: Microsoft Copilot's October roundup: Projects, role-based Cowork plugins and interactive slides
items.summary: October updates include merged Chat and Cowork navigation, Projects, role-based Cowork plugins, a SharePoint knowledge base, Excel clean-data skills, PowerPoint with Sonnet 5.5 and interactive slides, and Word legal skills with more than 20 purpose-built skills. Several items roll out in November, and Workspaces file editing arrives in January.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: try the interactive slides on a recurring status deck and see whether viewers click through.

sections.title: Funding
sections.description: Rounds confirmed against a company or lead-investor post.

items.title: Bedrock Robotics raises $600M Series C to retrofit excavators for autonomy
items.summary: CapitalG co-led Bedrock Robotics' $600 million Series C, and Bedrock says its kit connects to a machine's existing hydraulics so existing excavators can run with no one in the cab. Its software turns project plans or CAD files into tasks, and autonomous equipment began paid work on live commercial sites in August. TechCrunch reports a $4.1 billion valuation; the CapitalG post does not state it.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: watch for plan-to-task workflows that start from CAD files; the same idea fits any drawing-driven job.

items.title: Hex raises $100M at a $1.2B valuation and launches Hex 4.0, rebuilt for agents
items.summary: Hex announced a $100 million round at a $1.2 billion valuation led by Peak XV and 137 Ventures, alongside Hex 4.0, a from-scratch rewrite for agent-native analytics. Work is rooted in plain code rather than a proprietary YAML format.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask an analytics agent a question your dashboard cannot answer and see how it shows its work.

items.title: Hugging Face launches Project ProtoStar to make public science data AI-ready
items.summary: ProtoStar supports sharing publicly funded datasets, models and code in AI-ready formats on open infrastructure. Its first challenge, Climate Risk Intelligence, hosted by Carnegie Mellon University, runs November 2 to 13 and asks entrants to forecast four climate indicators for 210 U.S. cities. Hugging Face hosts more than 17,000 public datasets across core science domains.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: enter the climate challenge with a small internal team as a two-week sprint on building-relevant forecasting.

sections.title: To Watch
sections.description: Early programs and platforms with high signal.

items.title: Google opens a Connected Apps Platform to build once for Search and the Gemini app
items.summary: Developers can build Connected Apps once through a cloud MCP server or Android MCP with AppFunctions, then register, test and submit them in Google Connected Console. More than 50 Connected Apps are live; Adobe, Experian, Localiza and Peloton are live in Gemini, and Calm launches across both. Access is opening in phases.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: sketch the one small tool of yours that would be worth putting inside Gemini.

items.title: Anthropic's AI for Science program grows to 20 partners with free credits and a lab-instrument spec
items.summary: Anthropic is partnering with 20 foundations, institutions and research groups, including Simons Foundation, Schmidt Sciences, Wellcome Sanger Institute and the Francis Crick Institute, to provide free Claude credits for high-impact science, plus a discounted Team plan for scientists. The Model Hardware Standard, developed with HHMI Janelia, is a research-preview spec for AI agents to operate lab instruments.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: pitch a research group credits for one instrument-data project and see what an agent team does with it.

emerging_signals.pattern: Agents built for one medium are replacing general chat
emerging_signals.evidence: Riverside Agents for video, Canva Brush for design edits, Empacer for small-business tasks and Zest for group dining all launched within seven days.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether approval-first workflows stay the default as these tools gain autonomy.

emerging_signals.pattern: Chat windows are becoming file editors
emerging_signals.evidence: Gemini edits documents, PDFs, slides and sheets in place; Claude added Docs and Slides in September; Microsoft Copilot added interactive slides in October.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Which assistant first supports round-trip editing in all Office formats.

emerging_signals.evidence: Anthropic's drug-discovery post lists partner numbers; Hugging Face's ProtoStar opens a public climate forecasting challenge.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Independent replication of the antibody and CAR T results, and ProtoStar leaderboard results after November 13.

flagged_unverified.reason: Primary pages show earlier dates (GPT-6: October 7; Grok 4.7: September 22; Gemini 3.8 Live: September 15; Gemini app agent update: May 19; Maritime listed '23 days ago'). Excluded as outside the window.

flagged_unverified.claim: Serval $150M Series C, General Compute $100M Series A, Foundry Robotics $100M Series A, Dren Bio $350M, Kalshi $1B (Crunchbase weekly roundup, October 30).
flagged_unverified.reason: Only the Crunchbase roundup was read; company announcements were not retrieved, so they stay out of Funding. Kalshi is a prediction market, not an AI launch.
Confirmed by the company's own release, but it is a manufacturing accelerator and the AI link is thin, so it is held out of the Launches funding list.

suggested_refinements.notes: Source limits this week: Product Hunt returns 403 to automated HTTP checks, so Product Hunt pages were read through the page-fetch tool and maker sites checked with HTTP 200 (Canva and Ideogram sites also returned 403 to curl but rendered through the fetch tool; Ideogram's homepage does not mention Precise Edit, so its Product Hunt page is the primary link). Product Hunt figures are the weekly leaderboard score at fetch time, ranks 11 and below were not captured, and Canva Brush and Riverside figures are launch-day scores. Mistral Large 4 date comes from Mistral's RSS feed (October 29) because the post is undated. Confetti's date (October 31) comes from search metadata because the Launch YC page shows relative times. Gemini 4 Carbon benchmark claims are Google's own and Carbon access is limited at launch. Anthropic's S-1 filing (October 26) was left out as a corporate filing, not a product launch. Bedrock's $4.1B valuation appears in TechCrunch and not in CapitalG's post. Requested Sonnet 5.0 was unavailable; the closest current Sonnet (5.5) was used.
